title: Household drinking-water service coverage by country and place of residence
publisher: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme for Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene
population: Percentage of the population using the service within each residence group (total, urban, rural). Country and territory names and ISO3 identifiers come directly from JMP.

serviceDefinitions.safe: An improved drinking-water source on premises, available when needed, and free from faecal and priority chemical contamination.
serviceDefinitions.basic: An improved drinking-water source with a round-trip collection time of up to 30 minutes, including queuing. At least basic includes safely managed service.

methods: The workbook’s unformatted wat sheet provides the underlying estimates. The formatted Water sheet supplies presentation qualifiers. Both sheets are checked for matching ISO3, country name, year and service columns.
At least basic comes directly from the workbook’s cumulative wat_basal fields. Both indicators describe service levels and overlap.

The displayed gap is urban percentage minus rural percentage for the same country, year and service. National percentages are the published estimates. Each residence has its own population denominator.

CSV percentages retain the source cell’s decimal precision. Public source labels <1 and >99 are preserved separately, including when the underlying estimate equals zero or 100. The gap uses the underlying estimates before display rounding.
A dash on the formatted source sheet corresponds to a blank unformatted source cell. Downloaded CSV fields are empty for missing estimates and gaps. Only years found in the release are included.
